info.name: Uyir User Service
info.description:
userservice called **directly** (`{{baseUrl}}`, default http://localhost:8089) - patient profile, family members, medical records, health records from other services.

Requests send the identity headers the api-gateway sets after verifying the access token:

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `x-user-id` | `{{userId}}` - the token `sub`; a new uuid per run |
| `x-user-role` | `PATIENT` |
| `x-gateway-secret` | `{{gatewaySecret}}` - `GATEWAY_SECRET` from userservice/.env |

Run top to bottom. Errors are `{ error: { code, message } }`.

Through the gateway (bearer token instead of these headers) the same requests live in `api-gateway/postman/uyir-all-services.postman_collection.json` › *10 · User Service*.

Generated by `postman/generate.mjs` - edit that and re-run instead of editing this file.

item.name: Onboarding & profile
item.description: Signup does not touch userservice. After login the app calls `GET /me`; `404 PROFILE_REQUIRED` means show the *Create your profile* screen with the privacy notice (`GET /me/privacy`), which submits `POST /me` with the profile and `consent`. That creates the user (id = token `sub`), its patient number, the profile and the consent record in one go. Under-18s are refused (`403 MINOR_ACCOUNT`) - a parent adds them as a family member.

request.description: Starts the run as a brand-new patient (`userId` = a new uuid, standing in for the token `sub`).
The notice version (and URL, grievance officer) the app shows and the patient consents to. Works before onboarding.
Nothing is stored without consent to the privacy notice (DPDP Act).
`email` is required when the profile is created: `fieldErrors.email` = `["email is required."]`.

request.description: `referralCode` is at most 30 characters. A code the Health Partner service doesn't know is `400 INVALID_REFERRAL_CODE` (needs HP_SERVICE_URL; see docs/referrals.md).

item.name: Create profile with an unknown referral code (400 INVALID_REFERRAL_CODE)

exec: console.log("referralCode not set - skipping the HP code check");

request.description: The Health Partner service doesn't know the code: refused, and nothing is created, so the patient can correct it or leave it empty. Runs only when `referralCode` is set in the environment (that is, userservice is wired to the HP service with `HP_SERVICE_URL`) - without HP the code would be accepted unchecked.

`201 { user: { id, status, createdAt, patientNumber }, profile }`. `fullName`, `email` (stored trimmed and lower-case) and `consent` ({ noticeVersion, adultDeclaration: true }) are required. The user id is always the caller's - an `id` in the body is ignored.

Optional `referralCode` (at most 30 characters, any letter case; empty = none): the Health Partner who brought the patient in. Checked with the HP service (`400 INVALID_REFERRAL_CODE` if it doesn't know it, so the patient can correct it; accepted unchecked if HP is down or not configured). Only at creation. The HP earns ₹10 once the patient links their own ABHA - docs/referrals.md.

Here it is the environment's `referralCode` - a real HP's code to try the referral flow, or empty.
`privacy.consentRequired` true = show the notice again (it changed) and POST /me/consents.

Full replace - optional fields left out (here `phone`, `address`) are cleared, except `email`: left out keeps it, `null` clears it. Before onboarding a PUT creates the profile instead (`201`), like the old authservice endpoint.

item.name: Family members
item.description:
Records under the patient's account - they cannot log in. `relationship`: SPOUSE · FATHER · MOTHER · SON · DAUGHTER · BROTHER · SISTER · GRANDPARENT · GRANDCHILD · OTHER.

Adding one needs `consent` for that person: `basis` MEMBER_CONSENTED (an adult who agreed) or PARENT_OR_GUARDIAN (required for an under-18). A member without consent is listed with `consent.care: false` and their data stays hidden.

Add family member with unknown relationship (400)

Service-to-service read used by homebasedcare while it creates a FAMILY_MEMBER booking: `X-User-Id` only, no token. Only members with consent are returned. A patient who never onboarded gets `[]`.

item.name: Medical records
item.description:
Each record belongs to the patient (`familyMemberId: null`) or one of their family members. Create takes an optional `familyMemberId`; lists take `?memberId=self` or `?memberId=<family member id>` - without it you get the whole account.

Every read and change is written to the `access_audit` table.

item.name: Allergies
item.description: `category`: FOOD · DRUG · ENVIRONMENT · OTHER. `severity`: MILD · MODERATE · SEVERE.

item.name: Medications
item.description: `dosage` and `frequency` are free text. `endDate` may not be before `startDate`.

item.name: Add medication ending before it starts (400)
Vitals
item.description: `type`: BLOOD_PRESSURE (`value` = systolic, `secondaryValue` = diastolic) · HEART_RATE · BLOOD_SUGAR · SPO2 · TEMPERATURE · WEIGHT · HEIGHT. The service sets `unit` from the type. `measuredAt` (ISO 8601, not in the future) defaults to now. Readings can't be edited - delete and add again.

request.description: Newest `measuredAt` first.

item.name: Health records
item.description:
Records other services push (see `docs/health-records.md`), and the patient's combined medical history.

Producer requests need no token; the record's `source` names the producer.

request.description: `201 { outcome: "created", recordId }`. Kafka producers publish the same record to `health-records.events` instead.
Same `sourceVersion` - ignored, so re-delivery is harmless. A higher version replaces the record.
Filters: `memberId`, `recordType`, `source`, `from`, `to`, `limit`. Paged with `next.before` + `next.beforeId`.
Conditions, allergies, current medications, latest vital per type, recent provider records and the linked ABHA - one person at a time (`?memberId=self|<id>`).
Linking (`POST /me/abha/otp`, `POST /me/abha/verify`) needs ABDM credentials and a real ABHA, so it is not part of this run.

item.name: Privacy (DPDP Act)
item.description:
The patient's controls under the DPDP Act. Notice, consents, access log, sharing summary, export and erasure work whether or not the patient has consented or onboarded; the nominee needs the profile.

Consent purposes: `CARE` (store and use health data - required) · `ABDM_SHARING` (link an ABHA, share through ABDM). Withdrawing `CARE` for a family member erases them; `ABDM_SHARING` unlinks the ABHA; `CARE` for oneself is `DELETE /me`.

request.description: Needed before `POST /me/abha/otp`. For a family member add `memberId` and `basis` instead of `adultDeclaration`. `409 NOTICE_OUTDATED` when `noticeVersion` is not the current one.
Unlinks the ABHA (if any). `?memberId=<id>` for a family member.

item.name: ABHA creation
item.description:
Creates an ABHA for a patient who has none, by Aadhaar OTP, and links it. **Optional and separate from profile creation** - `POST /me` never calls ABDM. Self only for now; family members link an existing ABHA instead.

Flow: consent text → Aadhaar OTP → verify (ABHA created and linked, 201, `next`) → [mobile OTP + verify when `next` is `MOBILE_VERIFY`] → address suggestions → choose address. `next: DONE` means the Aadhaar already had an ABHA and it was linked.

The real steps run only when the environment sets `aadhaar` (secret) and, one at a time, `aadhaarOtp` / `mobileOtp` from the SMS - otherwise they are skipped. The Aadhaar number is never stored or logged by userservice.

Contract: `docs/abha-creation.md`.

item.description: Deletes what this run created. Deleting a family member also deletes their medical records. Ends by erasing the whole account.
